record.paper_title: Progress and open questions in the physics of neutrino cross sections at intermediate energies
record.original_question: How can nuclear dynamics, final-state interactions, and secondary production mechanisms be modeled with enough reliability that exclusive strangeness-production measurements on nuclear targets can be used to infer the corresponding elementary neutrino-nucleon strangeness-production reactions?

evidence.quote: For this reason, from the ongoing exclusive strangeness production measurements on nuclear targets at MINERνA, it will be very hard to extract the corresponding reactions on the nucleon, unless a very reliable modeling of the nuclear dynamics is implemented.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem of disentangling nuclear effects (initial-state nuclear dynamics, FSI, and secondary production) from neutrino-induced strangeness production on nuclei remains an active and open challenge in intermediate-energy neutrino physics. Recent reviews and MINERvA/T2K/MicroBooNE analyses (2020–2025) continue to highlight large model dependence and significant discrepancies between generators (GENIE, NuWro, NEUT, GiBUU) for strange final states, with no consensus reliable model yet established.

status_evidence.title: NuSTEC White Paper: Status and Challenges of Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering
status_evidence.snippet: Strangeness production on nuclei suffers from sizable nuclear effects (FSI, secondary hyperon/kaon production) that limit extraction of elementary cross sections.
status_evidence.claim: Modeling nuclear effects in strangeness production remains an open challenge.

status_evidence.title: MINERvA strange-particle production measurements
status_evidence.snippet: Comparisons to GENIE show substantial discrepancies attributable to FSI and secondary production modeling uncertainties.
status_evidence.claim: Reliable nuclear modeling for exclusive strangeness production is not yet achieved.
